newsitem.title: INDIA: Wobbly Indian stocks expect to slide this week.
newsitem.headline: Wobbly Indian stocks expect to slide this week.

text.p: Wobbly Indian stock markets are expected to slide this week on fears of an economic slowdown and sluggish growth in corporate earnings, brokers and analysts said on Sunday.
"The outlook is plagued by uncertainties and lack of investor interest -- you could expect a fall of 100-150 points," said Himanshu Kaji, chief executive officer at broking firm Mangaldas L. Kaji.
"Grim" was his answer when asked how he would characterise the outlook.

Last week, Bombay's benchmark 30-share index slumped 160.70 points, or 4.80 percent, to 3,347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs, including a waiver of a minimum corporate tax proposed in the government's July budget.
Kaji said the economy was slowing and corporate earnings growth in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) would ease to 10 to 15 percent against a more robust 25-30 percent a year ago.
The government aims for brisk 6.6 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) this year, but has said a slowdown in infrastructure growth could affect that target.
The market was also undermined by political uncertainties, traders said.

Charges of corruption against some leaders and officials of the previous Congress party government and talk of a Congress leadership crisis has put pressure on Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left government.
The ruling minority coalition's survival depends on the support of the Congress party.
"The market should begin (this week) on a sober note," Nucleus Securities said in a report. "We see the market drifting in (the) absence of any investment interest.
"We expect the market to be in the range of 3,250-3,425 points."
Activity will be hit by a two-day Hindu festival holiday at the Bombay Stock Exchange, the country's premier bourse, which is scheduled to resume trading on Wednesday.
Sudipto Datta, analyst at Calcutta broking firm C. Mackertich, said he expected shares to remain flat this week with foreign investors sidelined.
"I expect the rupee to depreciate nearly five percent by December," he told Reuters. "This could dampen foreign buying in the interim period."
Some strategists expect buying to pick up by the end of the month when attention turns to first-half corporate results.
"Automobile companies are expected show among the highest earnings growth across sectors for fiscal 1996/97," said Sangeeta Mehta, equity strategist at Kotak Securities.
Pharmaceuticals and stocks of fast moving consumer goods are also expected to report strong earnings growth, she said.

A corporate roadshow by the State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank which is raising $400 million through an issue of global depositary receipts, will also attract market attention, dealers said.
The stock has been sold heavily by foreign funds in the hope of buying the GDRs at a discount to the local price.
